01
Product Deconstruction & CAD Reconstruction
Anko Bluetooth Speaker

This project focused on the deconstruction and analysis of a small Bluetooth speaker to gain an understanding of its manufacturing and assembly processes. These findings informed a detailed evaluation of the speaker's design and supported the accurate recreation of the product through CAD modelling.

SolidWorks KeyShot Sketching Photoshop InDesign
In Context Use

Designed for portability and engaging audio-visual performance indoors, suited to homes, offices, and small gatherings — its vibrant lighting and low-cost materials target teenagers and young adults seeking affordable options.

Deconstruction & Components Analysis

A systematic teardown documented the fastening methods and spatial arrangement of the PCB, drivers, and housing. Draft angles and ejector-pin marks confirmed the product was optimised for high-volume injection-moulded tooling.

CAD Construction & Assembly

Every component was reconstructed in SolidWorks from measurements taken during teardown, with a full bill of materials and exploded diagram documenting build order and part accountability.

Final Renders

The completed CAD model rendered back into a studio product shot, reflecting the physical speaker's true proportions, finishes, and LED detailing.

Final Renders

A top-down view highlighting the perforated grille and radial LED ring, the speaker's key visual and interactive feature.

Exploded View

A fully exploded CAD view separating every internal part — grille, LED ring, foam padding, housing, battery, and PCB — in true assembly order.

02
User Experience & Interaction
Mid Century Modern Lamp

This project focused on creating an intuitive and experimental lighting product given a theme, with the focus on a tangible user interaction that drives a specific experience through mechanical, electronic, or physical means.

SolidWorks KeyShot Sketching Photoshop InDesign
Ideation

Concept sketches explored the Mid-Century Modern aesthetic — cantilevered structures and globular light sources characteristic of the era — before one direction was chosen for its balance of identity, usability, and feasibility.

Colour, Material & Finish

Reference imagery of mid-century interiors — walnut cabinetry, warm light — informed a CMF strategy pairing walnut with orange, white, brass, and opal glass.

Colour, Material & Finish

The finished CMF direction gives a premium yet soft, diffused ambient glow characteristic of 1950s and 60s lighting design.

Prototyping

Built through hands-on fabrication combining shaped wood and formed acrylic. Iterative testing refined the form, assembly, and integration of electronics into a functional, cohesive object.

Final Renders

The completed CAD model rendered in studio lighting, matching the finished prototype's proportions and warm CMF palette.

Final Renders

A macro view of the shade assembly — orange lacquer, white diffuser, and opal glass globe framed by a brass ring.

03
Product Redesign & Concept Ideation
BMW M8 Engine Cover Redesign

This project required redesigning the current BMW M8 Competition engine cover, reimagining it through the theme of Digital Design — balancing BMW's motorsport graphic identity with the aesthetics of digital hardware.

SolidWorks KeyShot Sketching Photoshop InDesign
Ideation

Three directions were explored for the redesign, aiming to reflect the vehicle's data-driven performance through asymmetric layering, circuit-inspired linework, and topology-driven forms.

In Context

The redesign blends seamlessly into the engine bay — the first focus point for the user — promoting a sporty, aggressive character that reinforces the M8 Competition's luxury performance identity.

Final Renders

Repeated trapezoidal forms and vertical orientation — consistent principles across BMW M models — were preserved to keep the redesign legible as BMW.

Final Renders

Matte finishes and machined surfaces build a high-end, refined aesthetic, with the M Power branding and tri-colour circuit graphic as the compositional anchor.

Final Renders

Carbon-fibre sections reduce visual weight against the matte black shell, echoing the tension between organic data-flow forms and hard geometric precision.

04
Concept Ideation & User Experience
Mini Scooter Concept

An exploration of a personal transportation vehicle with close consideration of ergonomics, human factors, and human-machine interaction. The challenge was translating MINI's automotive personality into a micromobility vehicle.

SolidWorks KeyShot Sketching Photoshop InDesign
Ideation

Using underlays, several scooter concepts were developed to keep MINI's design language close throughout. Tutor feedback on transportability, form, and function narrowed the field to one direction.

CMF & Aesthetics

A premium, lightweight construction with curated colourways gives each version a distinct personality for different user groups while maintaining brand consistency.

Prototyping

Small-scale FDM prints allowed quick ergonomic assessment before the final form was sanded, primed, and painted to represent the chosen CMF strategy.

Final Renders

The T-bar handlebar integrates a circular digital display and controls, translating MINI's dashboard language into a compact micromobility format.

Final Renders

The deck and wheel-cover silhouette echo MINI's automotive curves, finished in the brand's signature red over a cream underbody.

About

About Me

I am a fourth-year Industrial Design student at the Queensland University of Technology, originally from Brazil. I am driven by a curiosity for how products are made and how they can be improved, with a focus on user experience, attention to detail, innovation, and sustainability.

My work spans the full design process, from research and sketching to detailed CAD modelling, prototyping, and rendering. I aim to create products that are purposeful, intuitive, and manufacturable, balancing creative thinking with technical execution.

From a young age, I have been passionate about making and creating, which continues to shape my approach to design today.
